Adventure: The leads escape the final trap or natural danger, secure the key artifact or knowledge, and choose to value their hard-won bond over total riches.
They fail to claim the main treasure, but uncover a hidden truth or smaller relic that changes their lives and leaves the legend partially unresolved.
After returning from the expedition, they expose a corrupt patron or rival, restoring their reputations and setting up future adventures.
The ruin, fortress, or temple collapses or is sealed to prevent its power from being misused, and they walk away changed but alive.
The explorer and their former rival agree to continue working together as partners, hinting at more journeys to come.
The crew or team celebrates survival in a quiet moment, acknowledging losses and honoring those who didn’t make it back.
The map or clue that started the quest is passed on or destroyed, closing this chapter while new mysteries remain.
The once-skeptical character finally witnesses undeniable proof of the legend and embraces a more adventurous life.
They return the stolen or smuggled artifact to its rightful place, restoring balance to the region and ending a local curse or conflict.
The story closes on a distant glimpse of the unexplored horizon or a newly discovered clue, suggesting the world still holds deeper secrets.
Horror: One or two survivors escape the main haunted location, but a subtle final image or sound reveals the entity still exists and may follow.
The protagonists destroy or contain the source of the haunting, but at the cost of their sanity, freedom, or an important relationship.
They uncover the true origin of the curse or entity and pass the knowledge on, knowing that believing it is now someone else’s burden.
The haunting stops for now, but the final scene shows a child, object, or building beginning to behave in the same unsettling way.
A seemingly safe return to normal life is undercut by a small detail that proves the reality around them is permanently altered.
The location claiming the victims is left abandoned again, with warnings ignored while a new visitor approaches in the distance.
The main character chooses to stay behind or sacrifice themselves to hold the entity at bay, giving others a chance to escape.
Investigators capture evidence of the supernatural, but authorities dismiss it, leaving the characters isolated with what they know.
The nightmare finally ends for the characters, only for the last moment to reveal it was part of a larger, still-active pattern elsewhere.
The story ends on an ambiguous image or line of dialogue that lets the reader decide whether the horror was real, psychological, or both.
Fantasy: The leads survive the final confrontation and choose each other openly, even if their political or magical futures remain uncertain.
The dangerous artifact or magic is sealed, hidden, or willingly surrendered, and they accept a quieter but freer life together.
A corrupt ruler or faction falls, and the couple takes on new roles as protectors or reluctant leaders in a changing kingdom.
They stop the immediate threat but trigger a larger prophecy or balance shift, setting up new challenges beyond the story’s end.
The rebellion or conflict ends in fragile peace, and their relationship becomes a bridge between once-opposed sides.
One character returns to their old world or station while the other stays behind, with a clear promise or symbol tying them together.
Their bond stabilizes volatile magic or bloodline power, making them living anchors that keep the realm from tearing apart.
The story closes on a calm moment—on a balcony, in a field, or in a quiet village—where they finally rest and reflect on what changed.
Old obligations are resolved or broken, and they set off together toward an uncertain but shared future.
They choose duty over full union for now, but the final look, letter, or meeting makes clear their connection is enduring.
Monster: The surviving characters outsmart or trap the creature, leaving it buried, frozen, or sealed—though nature hints it might break free someday.
They manage to kill or neutralize the monster, but the cost in lives, habitat, or infrastructure makes the victory feel hollow.
The leads escape the disaster area but know authorities will cover up the truth, leaving them as the only witnesses.
The creature retreats to its domain, wounded but alive, and the final image shows that humans were the real intruders all along.
Evidence of the monster is lost or destroyed in the climax, and skeptics later rewrite events as a simple accident.
One character sacrifices themselves to distract or contain the creature long enough for others to get away.
Scientists or officials vow to study what remains more responsibly, while the last shot reveals a smaller offspring or spore surviving.
The leads leave the ruined facility, ship, or town behind, agreeing never to return and barely speaking of what happened.
The environment slowly recovers, but scars remain in the landscape and in the survivors’ relationships.
A final quiet scene juxtaposes normal life resuming with a subtle sign—distant tremor, shadow, or silhouette—that the threat is not extinct.
Science Fiction: The leads avert the immediate catastrophe and decide to keep working together in a new, more honest way.
They expose a hidden conspiracy or cover-up, forcing powerful institutions to change while knowing there will be backlash.
The dangerous experiment or technology is shut down or re-engineered with strict safeguards, and the protagonists become its wary guardians.
First contact or a strange signal is finally understood, and the story ends with a fragile but hopeful new relationship with the unknown.
The protagonists choose a morally difficult path—destroying data, abandoning a project, or leaving a colony—to prevent greater harm.
One character departs on a long mission while the other stays behind, and the ending centers on their promise to reconnect.
The crisis reveals that the AI, alien, or anomaly is not malicious but misinterpreted, and they negotiate a new coexistence.
They save the ship, station, or city but accept that the universe remains unpredictable and vast in ways they can’t fully control.
A recovered log, transmission, or journal entry frames the whole story in hindsight, hinting at how history will remember them.
The final scene zooms out from their personal resolution to show a larger cosmic or societal shift triggered by their actions.
Werewolf: The destined or hard-won bond between the two wolves is finally accepted, and they commit to facing pack politics and external threats together.
A hostile or rival pack is defeated or forced into truce, and their relationship becomes the cornerstone of a new balance between territories.
One of them chooses to step down from, or step into, leadership for the sake of both the pack’s safety and their bond.
The hidden or human life of one character is integrated with their wolf identity, and the couple finds a way to exist between both worlds.
An ancient law or tradition is challenged or rewritten so that their connection is no longer a source of shame or punishment.
They avert an impending war but accept that some alliances will always remain fragile, making their partnership even more vital.
A former enemy becomes a guarded ally, and the final scene shows mixed packs or outsiders beginning to coexist uneasily.
They choose to leave familiar territory together, founding or seeking a new pack where they can define their own rules.
The story ends on a moonlit patrol or run where their bond feels stable and instinctive, even if the future remains uncertain.
One character temporarily separates for duty or exile, but a clear, emotionally solid promise anchors their eventual return.
Superhero: The heroes defeat or neutralize the main threat, and the city gets a moment of calm while they finally acknowledge their connection out of costume.
A public battle forces one or both to partially reveal truths about themselves, but they gain new trust from each other and a select few allies.
They choose not to kill or permanently destroy the villain, instead opting for containment or rehabilitation, reflecting their shared values.
One character steps back from solo heroics to join or trust the other’s team, signaling a long-term partnership.
A new law, initiative, or alliance is formed between powered and non-powered people, with the couple as symbolic bridge figures.
The heroes save the day but accept ongoing misunderstandings or mistrust from the world, focusing instead on the trust between them.
A temporary separation is required for safety, time-travel, or multiversal reasons, but a final signal or token confirms their ongoing bond.
The epilogue shows them dealing with ordinary life problems while the super-threat recedes into the background.
A new, subtler threat is teased in the closing moments, and they prepare to face it together with a stronger, more honest partnership.
The story closes on a rooftop or quiet street scene where they watch over the city, united in purpose and feeling.
Romance: The pair openly choose each other and begin a committed relationship, with clear plans for how they’ll navigate work, family, or status conflicts.
They reconcile after a significant misunderstanding, addressing the root issues instead of glossing over them, and agree on new boundaries.
One or both characters decide to change careers, cities, or life paths so they can build a future that reflects what they genuinely want.
They don’t get together immediately but part on good terms, with a strong suggestion or specific plan that they’ll reconnect when the time is right.
A major external pressure is resolved or reduced, allowing their feelings room to breathe.
The finale centers on a quiet, grounded moment where they choose everyday intimacy over grand gestures.
They agree to slow down and rebuild trust after past hurt, showing that their happy ending is about doing the work, not just declaring love.
A rivalry or competition is resolved in a way where both keep their dignity and careers, proving they can win together rather than at each other’s expense.
A symbolic act marks the point where they start living for themselves, not just others.
The story closes on them supporting each other in a new endeavor, making it clear their relationship is a partnership rather than a distraction.
Crime: The leads survive the final job, heist, or showdown and choose to walk away from the criminal world together—or at least from their most dangerous roles.
One character takes a deal, confession, or fall to protect the other, leaving their future open but their loyalty unmistakable.
A powerful boss, fixer, or syndicate is taken down or weakened, and the protagonists carve out a smaller, more controlled life on the fringes.
They pull off the operation successfully but realize staying in that world will destroy them, and the ending focuses on their decision to disappear.
A journalist or investigator finally delivers the story, exposing corruption while accepting personal risk to their career or safety.
The uneasy alliance between law and underworld holds—for now—with the leads acting as a quiet line of communication between both sides.
A big score or cache is lost or deliberately destroyed so it can’t fuel further violence, leaving them with only what they can carry and each other.
Trust is rebuilt just enough for them to attempt a new start, whether that means going legitimate, changing cities, or laying low together.
The story ends with a morally gray but emotionally satisfying compromise: justice is partial, but the worst threats are removed.
A final scene shows the city’s criminal ecosystem shifting—new players rising, old ones gone—with a hint that the leads are done being pawns.
Action: The main threat is neutralized, and the leads finally let their guard down long enough to acknowledge their connection.
The protagonists refuse an offer to return to constant missions, choosing a more grounded life while knowing they can be called upon again if needed.
A corrupt official or organization behind the chaos is exposed, and the leads part ways professionally but remain in contact as trusted allies.
They complete the mission but at a personal cost—injury, reputation, or a broken tie—with the ending focusing on how they begin to heal together.
The once-reluctant partners now function as a seamless team and opt to keep working side by side in future operations.
A key location is saved or stabilized, and the closing moment shows ordinary people going about their lives because of the heroes’ work.
The pair choose to protect each other over finishing a perfect mission, signaling that their priorities have shifted from duty alone.
An epilogue jumps forward to show them in a calmer setting, with small echoes of their past missions still influencing how they live.
The final action beat is followed by a reflective beat where they decide what kind of lives they want after all this.
The story closes on a hint that a larger network, threat, or conspiracy is still out there, but the leads face it knowing they’ve already survived the worst together.
